13.34: And this thing turned to sinne unto the house of Jeroboam, even to root it out, and destroy it from the face of the earth.

14.1: At that time Abiiah the sonne of Jeroboam fell sick.
14.2: And Jeroboam said unto his wife, Up, I pray thee, and disguise thy self, that they know not that thou art the wife of Jeroboam, and goe to Shiloh: for there is Ahiiah the Prophet, which told mee that I should bee King over this people,
14.3: And take with thee tenne loaves and craknels, and a bottell of honie, and go to him: hee shall tell thee what shall become of the yong man.
14.4: And Ieroboams wife did so, and arose, and went to Shiloh, and came to the house of Ahiiah: but Ahiiah could not see, for his sight was decayed for his age.
14.5: Then the Lord said unto Ahiiah, Behold, the wife of Jeroboam cometh to ask a thing of thee for her sonne, for he is sick: thus and thus shalt thou say unto her: for when she cometh in, she shall feine her self to be another.
14.6: Therefore when Ahiiah heard the sound of her feet as she came in at the door, hee said, Come in, thou wife of Jeroboam: why feinest thou thus thy self to bee an other? I am sent to thee with heauie tidings.
14.7: Goe, tel Jeroboam, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Forasmuch as I have exalted thee from among the people, and have made thee prince over my people Israel,
14.8: And have rent the kingdom away from the house of David, and have given it thee, and thou hast not been as my servant David, which kept my commandements, and followed mee with all his heart, and did onely that which was right in mine eyes,
14.9: But hast done evil above al that were before thee (for thou hast gone and made thee other gods, and molten images, to provoke me, and hast cast me behind thy back)
14.10: Therefore behold, I will bring evil upon the house of Jeroboam, and will cut off from Jeroboam him that pisseth against the wall, aswell him that is shut up, as him that is left in Israel, and will sweep away the remnant of the house of Jeroboam, as a man sweepeth away doung, till it be all gone.
14.11: The dogges shall eat him of Ieroboams stock that dyeth in the citie, and the foules of the air shall eat him that dyeth in the field: for the Lord hath said it.
14.12: Up therefore and get thee to thine house: for when thy feet enter into the citie, the child shall die.
14.13: And al Israel shall mourn for him, and burie him: for he onely of Jeroboam shall come to the grave, because in him there is found some goodnes toward the Lord God of Israel in the house of Jeroboam.
14.14: Moreover, the Lord shall stirre him up a King over Israel, which shall destroy the house of Jeroboam in that day: what? yea, even now.
14.15: For the Lord shall smite Israel, as when a reed is shaken in the water, and hee shall weede Israel out of his good lad, which he gave to their fathers, and shall scatter them beyond the River, because they have made them groves, provoking the Lord to anger.
14.16: And he shall give Israel up, because of the sinnes of Jeroboam, who did sinne, and made Israel to sinne.
14.17: And Ieroboams wife arose, and departed, and came to Tirzah, and when she came to the threshold of the house, the yong man dyed,
14.18: And they buried him, and all Israel lamented him; according to the word of the Lord, which hee spake by the hand of his servant Ahiiah the Prophet.
14.19: And the rest of Ieroboams actes, how hee warred, and how hee reigned, behold, they are written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
14.20: And the dayes which Jeroboam reigned, were two and twentie yeere: and he slept with his fathers, and Nadab his sonne reigned in his stead.
14.21: Also Rehoboam the sonne of Salomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam was one and fourtie yere old, when he began to reign, and reigned seventeen yere in Jerusalem, the citie which the Lord did chuse out of al the tribes of Israel, to put his Name there: and his mothers name was Naamah an Ammonite.
14.22: And Judah wrought wickedness in the sight of the Lord: and they provoked him more with their sinnes, which they had committed, then all that which their fathers had done.
14.23: For they also made them hie places, and images, and groves on every hie hill, and under every green tree.
14.24: There were also Sodomites in the land, they did according to all the abominations of the nations, which the Lord had cast out before the children of Israel.
14.25: And in the fift yere of King Rehoboam, Shishak King of Egypt came up against Ierusale,
14.26: And took the treasures of the house of the Lord, and the treasures of the Kings house, and took away all: also he caried away all the shields of gold which Salomon had made.
14.27: And King Rehoboam made for them brasen shieldes, and committed them unto ye hands of the chief of the garde, which wayted at the door of the Kings house.
14.28: And when the King went into the house of the Lord, the garde bare them, and brought them again into the gard chamber.
14.29: And the rest of the actes of Rehoboam, and all that hee did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
14.30: And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.
14.31: And Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the citie of David: his mothers name was Naamah an Ammonite. And Abiiam his sonne reigned in his stead.

15.1: And in the eighteenth yeere of King Jeroboam the sonne of Nebat, reigned Abiiam over Judah.
15.2: Three yeere reigned hee in Jerusalem, and his mothers name was Maachah the daughter of Abishalom.
15.3: And hee walked in all the sinnes of his father, which hee had done before him: and his heart was not perfit with the Lord his God as the heart of David his father.
15.4: But for Dauids sake did the Lord his God give him a light in Jerusalem, and set up his sonne after him, and established Jerusalem,
15.5: Because David did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, and turned from nothing that he commanded him, all the dayes of his life, save onely in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
15.6: And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam as long as he lived.
15.7: The rest also of the actes of Abiiam, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah? there was also war between Abiiam, and Jeroboam.
15.8: And Abiiam slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the citie of David: and Asa his sonne reigned in his stead.
15.9: And in the twentie yeere of Jeroboam King of Israel reigned Asa over Judah.
15.10: He reigned in Jerusalem one and fourtie yeere, and his mothers name was Maachah the daughter of Abishalom.
15.11: And Asa did right in the eyes of the Lord, as did David his father.
15.12: And he took away the Sodomites out of the land, and put away all the idoles that his fathers had made.
15.13: And he put down Maachah his mother also from her estate, because she had made an idol in a grove: and Asa destroyed her idoles, and burnt them by the brook Kidron.
15.14: But they put not down the hie places. Neuertheles Asas heart was upright with the Lord all his dayes.
15.15: Also he brought in the holy vessels of his father, and the things that he had dedicated unto ye house of the Lord, silver, and gold, and vessels.
15.16: And there was war between Asa and Baasha King of Israel all their dayes.
15.17: Then Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah, and buylt Ramah, so that he would let none go out or in to Asa King of Judah.
15.18: Then Asa took all the silver and the gold that was left in the treasures of the house of the Lord, and the treasures of the kings house, and delivered them into the handes of his seruantes, and King Asa sent them to Ben-hadad the sonne of Tabrimon, the sonne of Hezion king of Aram that dwelt at Damascus, saying,
15.19: There is a covenant between me and thee, and between my father and thy father: behold, I have sent unto thee a present of silver and gold: come, break thy covenant with Baasha King of Israel, that he may depart from me.
15.20: So Ben-hadad hearkened unto King Asa, and sent the captaines of the hosts, which he had, against the cities of Israel, and smote lion, and Dan, and Abel-beth-maachah, and all Cinneroth, with all the land of Naphtali.
15.21: And when Baasha heard thereof, hee left buylding of Ramah, and dwelt in Tirzah.
15.22: Then king Asa assembled al Judah, none excepted. and they took the stones of Ramah, and the timber thereof, wherewith Baasha had buylt, and King Asa built with them Geba of Beniamin and Mizpah.
15.23: And the rest of all the actes of Asa, and all his might, and all that he did, and the cities which he buylt, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah? but in his old age he was diseased in his feet.
15.24: And Asa slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the citie of David his father. And Jehoshaphat his sonne reigned in his stead.
15.25: And Nadab the sonne of Jeroboam began to reign over Israel the second yere of Asa King of Judah, and reigned over Israel two yeere.
15.26: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, walking in the way of his father, and in his sinne wherewith he made Israel to sinne.
15.27: And Baasha the sonne of Ahijah of ye house of Issachar conspired against him, and Baasha slue him at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistims: for Nadab and all Israel layde siege to Gibbethon.
15.28: Even in the third yeere of Asa King of Judah did Baasha slay him, and reigned in his stead.
15.29: And when he was King, he smote all the house of Jeroboam, he left none alive to Jeroboam, until hee had destroyed him, according to the word of the Lord which he spake by his servant Ahijah the Shilonite,
15.30: Because of the sinnes of Jeroboam which he committed, and wherewith he made Israel to sinne, by his provocation, wherewith he provoked the Lord God of Israel.
15.31: And the residue of the actes of Nadab, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
15.32: And there was war between Asa and Baasha King of Israel, all their dayes.
15.33: In the third yeere of Asa King of Judah, began Baasha the sonne of Ahijah to reign over all Israel in Tirzah, and reigned four and twentie yeeres.
15.34: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, walking in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sinne, wherewith he made Israel to sinne.

16.1: Then the word of the Lord came to Jehu the sonne of Hanani against Baasha, saying,
16.2: Forasmuch as I exalted thee out of the dust, and made thee captain over my people Israel, and thou hast walked in the way of Jeroboam, and hast made my people Israel to sinne, to provoke me with their sinnes,
16.3: Behold, I will take away the posteritie of Baasha, and the posteritie of his house, and will make thine house like the house of Jeroboam the sonne of Nebat.
16.4: He that dyeth of Baashas stock in the citie, him shall the dogs eat: and that man of him which dyeth in the fieldes, shall the foules of the ayre eat.
16.5: And the rest of the actes of Baasha and what he did, and his power, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
16.6: So Baasha slept with his fathers, and was buryed in Tirzah, and Elah his sonne reigned in his stead.
16.7: And also by the hand of Jehu the sonne of Hanani the Prophet, came the word of the Lord to Baasha, and to his house, that he should be like the house of Jeroboam, even for all the wickednes that he did in the sight of the Lord, in provoking him with the work of his hands, and because he killed him.
16.8: In the six and twentie yeere of Asa king of Judah began Elah ye sonne of Baasha to reign over Israel in Tirzah, and reigned two yeere.
16.9: And his servant Zimri, captain of half his charets, conspired against him, as he was in Tirzah drinking, til he was drunken in the house of Arza steward of his house in Tirzah.
16.10: And Zimri came and smote him and killed him, in the seven and twentie yeere of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his stead.
16.11: And when he was King, and sat on his throne, he slew al the house of Baasha, not leaving thereof one to piss against a wall, neither of his kinsfolkes nor of his friendes.
16.12: So did Zimri destroy all the house of Baasha, according to the word of the Lord which he spake against Baasha by the hand of Jehu the Prophet,
16.13: For all the sinnes of Baasha, and sinnes of Elah his sonne, which they sinned and made Israel to sinne, and provoked the Lord God of Israel with their vanities.
16.14: And the rest of the actes of Elah, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
16.15: In the seven and twentie yeere of Asa King of Judah did Zimri reign seven dayes in Tirzah, and the people was then in camp against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistims.
16.16: And the people of the host heard say, Zimri hath conspired, and hath also slayne the King. Wherefore all Israel made Omri the captain of the host, king over Israel that same day, even in the host.
16.17: Then Omri went up from Gibbethon, and all Israel with him, and they besieged Tirzah.
16.18: And when Zimri saw, that the citie was taken, he went into the palace of the Kings house, and burnt himself, and the Kings house with fire, and so dyed,
16.19: For his sinnes which hee sinned, in doing that which is evil in the sight of the Lord, in walking in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sinnes which he did, causing Israel to sinne.
16.20: And the rest of the actes of Zimri, and his treason that hee wrought, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kinges of Israel?
16.21: Then were the people of Israel deuided into two partes: for half the people followed Tibni the sonne of Ginath to make him King, and the other half followed Omri.
16.22: But the people that folowed Omri, preuayled against the people that followed Tibni the sonne of Ginath: so Tibni dyed, and Omri reigned.
16.23: In the one and thirtie yeere of Asa King of Judah bega Omri to reign over Israel, and reigned twelve yeere. Six yeere reigned he in Tirzah.
16.24: And he bought the mountain Samaria of one Shemer for two talents of silver, and buylt in the mountain, and called the name of the citie, which he buylt, after the name of Shemer lord of the mountain, Samaria.
16.25: But Omri did evil in the eyes of the Lord, and did worse then all that were before him.
16.26: For he walked in all the way of Jeroboam the sonne of Nebat, and in his sinnes wherewith he made Israel to sinne in provoking the Lord God of Israel with their vanities.
16.27: And the rest of the actes of Omri, that hee did, and his strength that he shewed, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
16.28: And Omri slept with his fathers, and was buryed in Samaria: and Ahab his sonne reigned in his stead.
16.29: Now Ahab the sonne of Omri began to reign over Israel, in the eyght and thirtie yeere of Asa king of Judah: and Ahab the sonne of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria two and twenty yere.
16.30: And Ahab the sonne of Omri did worse in ye sight of the Lord then al that were before him.
16.31: For was it a light thing for him to walk in the sinnes of Jeroboam the sonne of Nebat, except hee took Jezebel also the daughter of Ethbaal King of the Zidonians to wife, and went and served Baal, and worshipped him?
16.32: Also he reared up an altar to Baal in the house of Baal, which he had buylt in Samaria.
16.33: And Ahab made a grove, and Ahab proceeded, and did provoke the Lord God of Israel more then all the kings of Israel that were before him.
16.34: In his dayes did Hiel the Bethelite buylde Jericho: he layed the foundation thereof in Abiram his eldest sonne, and set up the gates thereof in his yongest sonne Segub, according to the word of the Lord which he spake by Joshua the sonne of Nun.

17.1: And Eliiah the Tishbite one of the inhabitats of Gilead sayde unto Ahab, As the Lord God of Israel liveth, before whom I stand, there shall be neither dew nor rayne these yeeres, but according to my word.
17.2: And the word of the Lord came unto him, saying,
17.3: Go hence, and turn thee Eastward, and hide thy self in the river Cherith, that is over against Iorden,
17.4: And thou shalt drink of the river: and I have comanded the ravens to feed thee there.
17.5: So he went and did according unto the word of the Lord: for he went, and remained by the river Cherith that is over against Iorden.
17.6: And the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening, and he drank of the river.
17.7: And after a while the river dryed up, because there fell no rayne upon the earth.
17.8: And the word of the Lord came unto him, saying,
17.9: Up, and get thee to Zarephath, which is in Zidon, and remain there: behold, I have commanded a widow there to sustain thee.
17.10: So he arose, and went to Zarephath: and when he came to the gate of the citie, behold, the widow was there gathering stickes: and he called her, and sayde, Bring me, I pray thee, a litle water in a vessel, that I may drink.
17.11: And as she was going to fet it, he called to her, and sayde, Bring me, I pray thee, a morsel of bread in thine hand.
17.12: And she sayde, As the Lord thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but even an handful of meal in a barrel, and a litle oyle in a cruse: and behold, I am gathering a few stickes for to go in, and dress it for me and my sonne, that we may eat it, and dye.
17.13: And Eliiah said unto her, Fear not, come, do as thou hast sayd, but make me thereof a litle cake first of all, and bring it unto mee, and afterward make for thee, and thy sonne.
17.14: For thus saith the Lord God of Israel, The meal in the barrel shall not be wasted, neither shall the oyle in the cruse be diminished, unto the time that the Lord send rayne upon the earth.
17.15: So she went, and did as Eliiah sayd, and she did eat: so did he and her house for a certain time.
17.16: The barrell of the meal wasted not, nor the oyle was spent out of the cruse, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake by the hand of Eliiah.
17.17: And after these things, the sonne of the wife of the house fell sick, and his sickness was so sore, that there was no breath left in him.
17.18: And she said unto Eliiah, What have I to do with thee, O thou man of God? art thou come unto me to call my sinne to remembrance, and to slay my sonne?
17.19: And he said unto her, Give me thy sonne. and he took him out of her bosom, and caryed him up into a chamber, where he abode, and laid him upon his own bed.
17.20: Then he called unto the Lord, and sayde, O Lord my God, hast thou punished also this widow, with whom I soiourne, by killing her sonne?
17.21: And he stretched himself upon the child three times, and called unto the Lord, and said, O Lord my God, I pray thee, let this childes soul come into him again.
17.22: Then the Lord heard the voyce of Eliiah, and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived.
17.23: And Eliiah took the child, and brought him down out of the chamber into the house, and delivered him unto his mother, and Eliiah sayd, Behold, thy sonne liveth.
17.24: And the woman said unto Eliiah, Now I know that thou art a man of God, and that the word of the Lord in thy mouth is true.

18.1: After many dayes, the word of the Lord came to Eliiah, in the third yeere, saying, Goe, shew thy self unto Ahab, and I will send rayne upon the earth.
18.2: And Eliiah went to shew himself unto Ahab, and there was a great famine in Samaria.
18.3: And Ahab called Obadiah the gouernour of his house: (and Obadiah feared God greatly:
18.4: For when Jezebel destroyed the Prophets of the Lord, Obadiah took an hundreth Prophets, and hid them, by fiftie in a cave, and he fed them with bread and water.)
18.5: And Ahab said unto Obadiah, Goe into the land, unto all the fountaines of water, and unto all the rivers, if so be that we may find grass to save the horses and the mules alive, lest we depriue the land of the beastes.
18.6: And so they deuided the land between them to walk thorowe it. Ahab went one way by him self, and Obadiah went another way by him self.
18.7: And as Obadiah was in the way, behold, Eliiah met him: and he knew him, and fell on his face, and said, Art not thou my lord Eliiah?
18.8: And he answered him, Yea, goe tell thy lord, Behold, Eliiah is here.
18.9: And he said, What have I sinned, that thou wouldest deliver thy servant into the hand of Ahab, to slay me?
18.10: As the Lord thy God liveth, there is no nation or kingdom, whither my lord hath not sent to seek thee: and when they sayd, He is not here, he took an othe of the kingdom and nation, if they had not found thee.
18.11: And now thou sayest, Goe, tell thy lord, Behold, Eliiah is here.
18.12: And when I am gone from thee, the Spirit of the Lord shall cary thee into some place that I doe not know: so when I come and tell Ahab, if he cannot find thee, then wil he kill me: But I thy servant fear the Lord from my youth.
18.13: Was it not told my lord, what I did when Jezebel slew the Prophets of the Lord, how I hid an hundreth men of the Lordes Prophets by fifties in a cave, and fed them with bread and water?
18.14: And now thou sayest, Go, tel thy lord, Behold, Eliiah is here, that he may slay me.
18.15: And Eliiah said, As the Lord of hostes liveth, before whom I stand, I will surely shew my self unto him this day.
18.16: So Obadiah went to meet Ahab, and told him: And Ahab went to meet Eliiah.
18.17: And when Ahab saw Eliiah, Ahab said unto him, Art thou he that troubleth Israel?
18.18: And he answered, I have not troubled Israel, but thou, and thy fathers house, in that ye have forsaken the commandements of the Lord, and thou hast followed Baalim.
18.19: Now therefore send, and gather to me all Israel unto mount Carmel, and the prophets of Baal four hundreth and fiftie, and the prophets of the groves four hundreth, which eat at Iezebels table.
18.20: So Ahab sent unto all the children of Israel, and gathered the prophets together unto mount Carmel.
18.21: And Eliiah came unto all the people, and said, How long halt ye between two opinions? If the Lord be God, follow him: but if Baal be he, then goe after him. And the people answered him not a word.
18.22: Then said Eliiah unto the people, I onely remayne a Prophet of the Lord: but Baals prophets are four hundreth and fiftie men.
18.23: Let them therefore give us two bullockes, and let them chuse the one, and cut him in pieces, and lay him on the wood, but put no fire under, and I will prepare the other bullock, and lay him on the wood, and will put no fire under.
18.24: Then call ye on the name of your god, and I will call on the name of the Lord: and then the God that answereth by fire, let him be God. And all the people answered, and sayde, It is well spoken.
18.25: And Eliiah said unto the prophets of Baal, Chuse you a bullock, and prepare him first, (for ye are many) and call on the name of your gods, but put no fire under.
18.26: So they took the one bullock, that was given them, and they prepared it, and called on the name of Baal, from morning to noon, saying, O Baal, hear us: but there was no voyce, nor any to answer: and they leapt upon the altar that was made.
18.27: And at noon Eliiah mocked them, and said, Cry loud: for he is a god: either he talketh or pursueth his enemies, or is in his journey, or it may be that he sleepeth, and must be awaked.
18.28: And they cryed loud, and cut them selves as their maner was, with knives and launcers, till the blood gushed out upon them.
18.29: And when midday was passed, and they had prophecied until the offring of the evening sacrifice, there was neither voyce, nor one to answer, nor any that regarded.
18.30: And Eliiah said unto all the people, Come to me. And all the people came to him. And he repayred the altar of the Lord that was broken down.
18.31: And Eliiah took twelve stones, according to the nomber of the tribes of the sonnes of Iaakob, (unto whom the word of the Lord came, saying, Israel shalbe thy name)
18.32: And with the stones he buylt an altar in the Name of the Lord: and he made a ditch round about the altar, as great as would conteine two measures of seed.
18.33: And he put the wood in order, and hewed the bullock in pieces, and layd him on the wood,
18.34: And said, Fill four barrels with water, and powre it on the burnt offring and on the wood. Again he said, Doe so again. And they did so the second time. And he sayde, Doe it the third time. And they did it the third time.
18.35: And the water ran round about the altar: and he filled the ditch with water also.
18.36: And when they should offer the evening sacrifice, Eliiah the Prophet came, and sayd, Lord God of Abraham, Izhak and of Israel, let it be knowen this day, that thou art the God of Israel, and that I am thy servant, and that I have done all these things at thy commandement.
18.37: Hear me, O Lord, hear me, and let this people know that thou art the Lord God, and that thou hast turned their heart again at the last.
18.38: Then the fire of the Lord fell, and consumed the burnt offring, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water that was in the ditch.
18.39: And when all the people saw it, they fell on their faces, and said, The Lord is God, the Lord is God.
18.40: And Elijah said unto them, Take the prophets of Baal, let not a man of them escape. and they took them, and Eliiah brought them to the brook Kishon, and slew them there.
18.41: And Eliiah sayde unto Ahab, Get thee up, eat and drink, for there is a sound of much rayne.
18.42: So Ahab went up to eat and to drink, and Eliiah went up to the top of Carmel: and he crouched unto the earth, and put his face between his knees,
18.43: And sayde to his servant, Goe up now and look toward the way of the Sea. And he went up, and looked, and sayde, There is nothing. Again he sayd, Goe again seven times.
18.44: And at the seventh time he sayd, Behold, there ariseth a litle cloud out of the sea like a mans hand. Then he sayd, Up, and say unto Ahab, Make readie thy charet, and get thee down, that the rain stay thee not.
18.45: And in the mean while the heaven was black with cloudes and wind, and there was a great rayne. Then Ahab went up and came to Izreel.
18.46: And the hand of the Lord was on Eliiah, and he girded up his Ioynes, and ran before Ahab till he came to Izreel.

19.1: Now Ahab told Jezebel all that Eliiah had done, and how he had slain all the prophets with the sword.
19.2: Then Jezebel sent a messenger unto Eliiah, saying, The gods doe so to me and more also, if I make not thy life like one of their lives by to morowe this time.
19.3: When he saw that, he arose, and went for his life, and came to Beer-sheba, which is in Judah, and left his servant there.
19.4: But he went a dayes journey into the wilderness, and came and sat down under a juniper tree, and desired that he might die, and sayde, It is now ynough: O Lord, take my soul, for I am no better then my fathers.
19.5: And as he lay and slept under the juniper tree, behold now, an Angel touched him, and said unto him, Up, and eat.
19.6: And when he looked about, behold, there was a cake baken on the coles, and a pot of water at his head: so he did eat and drink, and returned and slept.
19.7: And the Angel of the Lord came again the second time, and touched him, and sayd, Up, and eat: for thou hast a great journey.
19.8: Then he arose, and did eat and drink, and walked in the strength of that meat fourtie dayes and fourtie nights, unto Horeb the mount of God.
19.9: And there he entred into a cave, and lodged there: and behold, the Lord spake to him, and said unto him, What doest thou here, Eliiah?
19.10: And he answered, I have been very ielous for the Lord God of hostes: for the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, broken down thine altars, and slayne thy Prophets with the sword, and I onely am left, and they seek my life to take it away.
19.11: And he said, Come out, and stand upon the mount before the Lord. And behold, the Lord went by, and a mightie strong wind rent the mountaines, and brake the rockes before the Lord: but the Lord was not in the wind: and after the wind came an earthquake: but the Lord was not in the earthquake:
19.12: And after the earthquake came fire: but the Lord was not in the fire: and after the fire came a still and soft voyce.
19.13: And when Eliiah heard it, he covered his face with his mantel, and went out, and stood in the entring in of ye cave: and behold, there came a voyce unto him, and sayd, What doest thou here, Eliiah?
19.14: And he answered, I have been very ielous for the Lord God of hostes, because the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, cast down thine altars, and slayne thy Prophets with the sword, and I onely am left, and they seek my life to take it away.
19.15: And the Lord said unto him, Goe, return by the wildernes unto Damascus, and when thou comest there, anoint Hazael King over Aram.
19.16: And Jehu the sonne of Nimshi shalt thou anoynt King over Israel: and Elisha the sonne of Shaphat of Abel Meholah shalt thou anoynt to be Prophet in thy roume.
19.17: And him that escapeth from the sword of Hazael, shall Jehu slay: and him that escapeth from the sword of Jehu, shall Elisha slay.
19.18: Yet wil I leave seven thousand in Israel, even all the knees that have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth that hath not kissed him.
19.19: So he departed thence, and found Elisha the sonne of Shaphat who was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen before him, and was with the twelft: and Eliiah went towards him, and cast his mantel upon him.
19.20: And he left the oxen, and ran after Eliiah, and sayde, Let mee, I pray thee, kiss my father and my mother, and then I wil follow thee. Who answered him, Go, return: for what have I done to thee?
19.21: And when he went back again from him, he took a couple of oxen, and slew them, and sod their flesh with the instruments of the oxen, and gave unto the people, and they did eat: then he arose and went after Eliiah, and ministred unto him.

20.1: Then Ben-hadad the King of Aram assembled all his armie, and two and thirtie Kings with him, with horses, and charets, and went up and besieged Samaria, and fought against it.
20.2: And he sent messengers to Ahab King of Israel, into the citie,
20.3: And sayd unto him, Thus sayth Ben-hadad, Thy silver and thy gold is mine: also thy women, and thy fayre children are mine.
20.4: And the King of Israel answered, and sayd, My lord King, according to thy saying, I am thine, and all that I have.
20.5: And when the messengers came again, they said, Thus commandeth Ben-hadad, and saith, When I shall send unto thee, and command, thou shalt deliver me thy silver and thy gold, and thy women, and thy children,
20.6: Or els I will send my servants unto thee by to morow this time: and they shall search thine house, and the houses of thy servants: and whatsoever is pleasant in thine eyes, they shall take it in their handes, and bring it away.
20.7: Then the King of Israel sent for all the Elders of the land, and sayd, Take heed, I pray you, and see how he seeketh mischief: for he sent unto me for my wives, and for my children, and for my silver, and for my gold, and I denyed him not.
20.8: And all the Elders, and all the people sayd to him, Hearken not unto him, nor consent.
20.9: Wherefore hee sayde unto the messengers of Ben-hadad, Tell my lord the King, All that thou diddest send for to thy servant at the first time, that I will doe, but this thing I may not do. And the messengers departed, and brought him an answer.
20.10: And Ben-hadad sent unto him, and sayde, The gods do so to me and more also, if the dust of Samaria be ynough to all the people that follow me, for every man an handful.
20.11: And the King of Israel answered, and sayd, Tell him, Let not him that girdeth his harneis, boast himself, as he that putteth it off.
20.12: And when he heard that tidings, as he was with the Kings drinking in the pavilions, he sayd unto his servants, Bring forth your engines, and they set them against the citie.
20.13: And behold, there came a Prophet unto Ahab King of Israel, saying, Thus sayeth the Lord, Hast thou seen all this great multitude? behold, I will deliver it into thine hand this day, that thou mayest know, that I am the Lord.
20.14: And Ahab sayd, By whom? And he sayde, Thus sayth the Lord, By the servants of the princes of the provinces. He sayde again, Who shall order the battel? And he answered, Thou.
20.15: Then he nombred the seruantes of the princes of the provinces, and they were two hundreth, two and thirtie: and after them he nombred the whole people of all the children of Israel, even seven thousand.
20.16: And they went out at noon: but Ben-hadad did drink till he was drunken in the tentes, both he and the Kings: for two and thirtie Kings helped him.
20.17: So the servants of the princes of the provinces went out first: and Ben-hadad sent out, and they shewed him, saying, There are men come out of Samaria.
20.18: And he sayde, Whether they be come out for peace, take them alive: or whether they bee come out to fight, take them yet alive.
20.19: So they came out of the citie, to wit, the servants of the princes of the provinces, and the host which followed them.
20.20: And they slew every one his enemie: and the Aramites fled, and Israel pursued them: but Ben-hadad ye King of Aram escaped on an horse with his horsemen.
20.21: And the King of Israel went out, and smote the horses and charets, and with a great slaughter slew he the Aramites.
20.22: (For there had come a Prophet to the King of Israel, and had sayd unto him, Goe, be of good courage, and consider, and take heed what thou doest: for when the yeere is gone about, the King of Aram wil come up against thee)
20.23: Then the servants of the King of Aram said unto him, Their gods are gods of the moutaines, and therefore they overcame us: but let us fight against them in the playne, and doubtless we shall overcome them.
20.24: And this doe, Take the Kings away, every one out of his place, and place captaines for them.
20.25: And nomber thy self an armie, like the armie that thou hast lost, with such horses, and such charets, and we wil fight against them in the plain, and doubtless we shall overcome them: and he hearkened unto their voyce, and did so.
20.26: And after the yeere was gone about, Ben-hadad nombred the Aramites, and went up to Aphek to fight against Israel.
20.27: And the children of Israel were nombred, and were all assembled and went against them, and the children of Israel pitched before them, like two litle flockes of kiddes: but the Aramites filled the countrey.
20.28: And there came a man of God, and spake unto the King of Israel, saying, Thus sayeth the Lord, Because the Aramites have sayd, The Lord is the God of the mountaines, and not God of the valleis, therefore will I deliver all this great multitude into thine hand, and ye shall know that I am the Lord.
20.29: And they pitched one over against the other seven dayes, and in the seventh day the battel was ioyned: and the children of Israel slew of the Aramites an hundreth thousand footemen in one day.
20.30: But the rest fled to Aphek into the citie: and there fel a wall upon seven and twentie thousand men that were left: and Ben-hadad fled into the citie, and came into a secret chamber.
20.31: And his servants sayd unto him, Behold now, we have heard say that the Kings of the house of Israel are merciful Kings: we pray thee, let us put sack cloth about our loynes, and ropes about our heads, and goe out to the King of Israel: it may be that he will save thy life.
20.32: Then they gyrded sackecloth about their loynes, and put ropes about their heads, and came to the King of Israel, and sayd, Thy servant Ben-hadad sayth, I pray thee, let me live: and he sayd, Is he yet alive? he is my brother.
20.33: Now the men took diliget heed, if they could catch any thing of him, and made haste, and sayd, Thy brother Ben-hadad. And he sayd, Go, bring him. So Ben-hadad came out unto him, and he caused him to come up unto the chariot.
20.34: And Ben-hadad sayd unto him, The cities, which my father took from thy father, I wil restore, and thou shalt make streetes for thee in Damascus, as my father did in Samaria. Then said Ahab, I will let thee goe with this covenant. So he made a covenant with him, and let him goe.
20.35: Then a certain man of the children of the Prophets sayd unto his neighbour by the comandement of the Lord, Smite me, I pray thee. But the man refused to smite him.
20.36: Then sayd he unto him, Because thou hast not obeyed the voyce of the Lord, behold, as soon as thou art departed from me, a lyon shall slay thee. So when he was departed from him, a lyon found him and slew him.
20.37: Then he found another man, and sayde, Smite mee, I pray thee. And the man smote him, and in smiting wounded him.
20.38: So the Prophet departed, and wayted for the King by the way, and disguised himself with ashes upon his face.
20.39: And when the King came by, he cried unto the King, and said, Thy servant went into the middes of the battel: and behold, there went away a man, whom another man brought unto me, and sayd, Keep this man: if he be lost, and want, thy life shall go for his life, or els thou shalt pay a talent of silver.
20.40: And as thy servant had here and there to do, he was gone: And the King of Israel said unto him, So shall thy iudgement be: thou hast given sentence.
20.41: And hee hasted, and took the ashes away from his face: and the King of Israel knew him that he was of the Prophets:
20.42: And he said unto him, Thus saith the Lord, Because thou hast let goe out of thine handes a man whom I appoynted to dye, thy life shall goe for his life, and thy people for his people.
20.43: And the King of Israel went to his house heauie and in displeasure, and came to Samaria.

21.1: After these things Naboth the Izreelite had a vineyard in Izreel, hard by the palace of Ahab King of Samaria.
21.2: And Ahab spake unto Naboth, saying, Give me thy vineyard, that I may make mee a garden of herbes thereof, because it is neere by mine house: and I will give thee for it a better vineyard then it is: or if it please thee, I will give thee the worth of it in money.
21.3: And Naboth said to Ahab, The Lord keep me from giving the inheritance of my father unto thee.
21.4: Then Ahab came into his house heauie and in displeasure, because of the word which Naboth the Izreelite had spoken unto him. for hee had sayde, I will not give thee the inheritance of my fathers, and he lay upon his bed, and turned his face and would eat no bread.
21.5: Then Jezebel his wife came to him and said unto him, Why is thy spirit so sad that thou eatest no bread?
21.6: And he said unto her, Because I spake unto Naboth the Izreelite, and sayd unto him, Give me thy vineyard for money, or if it please thee, I will give thee another vineyard for it: but he answered, I wil not give thee my vineyard.
21.7: Then Jezebel his wife sayde unto him, Doest thou now govern the kingdom of Israel? up, eat bread, and be of good cheer, I will give thee the vineyard of Naboth the Izreelite.
21.8: So she wrote letters in Ahabs name, and sealed them with his seal, and sent the letters unto the Elders, and to the nobles that were in his citie dwelling with Naboth.
21.9: And she wrote in the letters, saying, Proclaim a fast, and set Naboth among the chief of the people,
21.10: And set two wicked men before him, and let them witness against him, saying, Thou diddest blaspheme God and the King: then cary him out, and stone him that he may dye.
21.11: And the men of his citie, even the Elders and gouernours, which dwelt in his citie, did as Jezebel had sent unto them: as it was written in the letters, which she had sent unto them.
21.12: They proclaimed a fast, and set Naboth among the chief of the people,
21.13: And there came two wicked men, and sat before him: and the wicked men witnessed against Naboth in the presence of the people saying, Naboth did blaspheme God and the King. Then they caried him away out of the citie, and stoned him with stones, that he dyed.
21.14: Then they sent to Jezebel, saying, Naboth is stoned and is dead.
21.15: And when Jezebel heard that Naboth was stoned and was dead, Jezebel sayd to Ahab, Up, and take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Izreelite, which he refused to give thee for money: for Naboth is not alive, but is dead.
21.16: And when Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, he rose to go down to the vineyard of Naboth the Izreelite, to take possession of it.
21.17: And the word of the Lord came unto Eliiah the Tishbite, saying,
21.18: Arise, goe down to meet Ahab King of Israel, which is in Samaria. loe, he is in the vineyard of Naboth, whither he is gone down to take possession of it.
21.19: Therefore shalt thou say unto him, Thus sayth the Lord, Hast thou killed, and also gotten possession? And thou shalt speak unto him, saying, Thus sayth the Lord, In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth, shall dogs lick even thy blood also.
21.20: And Ahab sayd to Eliiah, Hast thou found mee, O mine enemie? And he answered, I have found thee: for thou hast sold thy self to work wickednes in the sight of the Lord.
21.21: Behold, I will bring evil upon thee, and wil take away thy posteritie, and wil cut off from Ahab him that pisseth against the wall, as well him that is shut up, as him that is left in Israel,
21.22: And I wil make thine house like the house of Jeroboam the sonne of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the sonne of Ahiiah, for the provocation wherewith thou hast provoked, and made Israel to sinne.
21.23: And also of Jezebel spake the Lord, saying, The dogs shall eat Jezebel, by the wall of Izreel.
21.24: The dogs shall eat him of Ahabs stock, that dyeth in the citie: and him that dyeth in the fieldes, shall the foules of the ayre eat.
21.25: (But there was none like Ahab, who did fell him self, to work wickedness in the sight of the Lord: whom Jezebel his wife provoked.
21.26: For he did exceeding abominably in following idoles, according to all that the Amorites did, whom the Lord cast out before the children of Israel.)
21.27: Now when Ahab heard those wordes, he rent his clothes, and put sackcloth upon him and fasted, and lay in sackecloth and went softely.
21.28: And the word of the Lord came to Eliiah the Tishbite, saying,
21.29: Seest thou how Ahab is humbled before me? because he submitteth himself before me, I will not bring that evil in his dayes, but in his sonnes dayes wil I bring evil upon his house.

22.1: And they continued three yeere without war between Aram and Israel.
22.2: And in the third yeere did Jehoshaphat the King of Judah come down to ye King of Israel.
22.3: (Then the King of Israel said unto his servants, Know yee not that Ramoth Gilead was ours? and wee stay, and take it not out of ye hand of the King of Aram?)
22.4: And he sayde unto Jehoshaphat, Wilt thou goe with mee to battel against Ramoth Gilead? And Jehoshaphat said unto the King of Israel, I am as thou art, my people as thy people, and mine horses as thine horses.
22.5: Then Jehoshaphat said unto the King of Israel, Ask counsaile, I pray thee, of the Lord to day.
22.6: Then the King of Israel gathered the prophets upon a four hundreth men, and said unto them, Shal I go against Ramoth Gilead to battel, or shall I let it alone? And they said, Go up: for ye Lord shall deliver it into the hands of the King.
22.7: And Jehoshaphat said, Is there here never a Prophet of the Lord more, that we might inquire of him?
22.8: And the King of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, There is yet one man (Michaiah the sonne of Imlah) by whom we may ask counsel of the Lord, but I hate him: for he doeth not prophecie good unto me, but evil. And Jehoshaphat sayd, Let not the King say so.
22.9: Then the King of Israel called an Eunuch, and sayde, Call quickely Michaiah the sonne of Imlah.
22.10: And the King of Israel and Jehoshaphat the King of Judah sat either of them on his throne in their apparell in the voyde place at the entring in of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets prophecied before them.
22.11: And Zidkiiah the sonne of Chenaanah made him hornes of yron, and sayd, Thus sayth the Lord, With these shalt thou push the Aramites, until thou hast consumed them.
22.12: And all the prophets prophecied so, saying, Goe up to Ramoth Gilead, and prosper: for the Lord shall deliver it into the Kings hand.
22.13: And the messenger that was gone to call Michaiah spake unto him, saying, Behold now, the wordes of the prophets declare good unto the King with one accord: let thy word therefore, I pray thee, be like the word of one of them, and speak thou good.
22.14: And Michaiah said, As the Lord liveth, whatsoever the Lord sayth unto me, that will I speak.
22.15: So he came to the King, and the King said unto him, Michaiah, shall we go against Ramoth Gilead to battel, or shall we leave off? And he answered him, Goe up, and prosper: and the Lord shall deliver it into the hand of the King.
22.16: And the King said unto him, How oft shall I charge thee, that thou tell me nothing but that which is true in the Name of the Lord?
22.17: Then he said, I saw all Israel scattered upon the mountaines, as sheep that had no shepheard. And the Lord sayde, These have no master, let every man return unto his house in peace.
22.18: (And the King of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, Did I not tell thee, that he would prophecie no good unto me, but evil?)
22.19: Again he said, Hear thou therefore the word of the Lord. I saw the Lord sit on his throne, and all the host of heaven stood about him on his right hand and on his left hand.
22.20: And the Lord sayd, Who shall entise Ahab that he may go and fall at Ramoth Gilead? And one said on this maner, and another sayd on that maner.
22.21: Then there came forth a spirit, and stood before the Lord, and sayd, I wil entise him. And the Lord sayd unto him, Wherewith?
22.22: And he sayd, I will goe out, and be a false spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. Then he sayd, Thou shalt entise him, and shalt also preuayle: goe forth, and doe so.
22.23: Now therefore behold, the Lord hath put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these thy prophets, and the Lord hath appoynted evil against thee.
22.24: Then Zidkiiah the sonne of Chenaanah came neere, and smote Michaiah on the cheek and sayd, When went the Spirit of the Lord from me, to speak unto thee?
22.25: And Michaiah said, Behold, thou shalt see in that day, when thou shalt goe from chamber to chamber to hide thee.
22.26: And the King of Israel sayd, Take Michaiah, and cary him unto Amon the gouernour of the citie, and unto Joash the Kings sonne,
22.27: And say, Thus saith the King, Put this man in the prison house, and feed him with bread of affliction, and with water of affliction, until I return in peace.
22.28: And Michaiah sayde, If thou return in peace, the Lord hath not spoken by me. And he sayd, Hearken all ye people.
22.29: So the King of Israel and Jehoshaphat the King of Judah went up to Ramoth Gilead.
22.30: And the King of Israel sayde to Jehoshaphat, I will change mine apparell, and will enter into the battell, but put thou on thine apparell. And the King of Israel changed himself, and went into the battel.
22.31: And the King of Aram commanded his two and thirtie captaines over his charets, saying, Fight neither with small, nor great, save onely against the King of Israel.
22.32: And when the captaines of the charets saw Jehoshaphat, they sayd, Surely it is the King of Israel, and they turned to fight against him: and Jehoshaphat cryed.
22.33: And when the captaines of the charets saw that he was not the King of Israel, they turned back from him.
22.34: Then a certain man drew a bow mightily and smote the King of Israel between the ioyntes of his brigandine. Wherefore he sayde unto his charet man, Turn thine hand and cary me out of the host: for I am hurt.
22.35: And the battel encreased that day, and the King stood still in his charet against the Aramites, and dyed at even: and the blood ran out of the wound into the middes of the charet.
22.36: And there went a proclamation thorowout the host about the going down of the sunne, saying, Every man to his citie, and every man to his own countrey.
22.37: So the King died, and was brought to Samaria, and they buried the King in Samaria.
22.38: And one washed the charet in the pool of Samaria, and the dogs licked up his blood (and they washed his armour) according unto the word of the Lord which he spake.
22.39: Concerning the rest of the actes of Ahab and all that he did, and the yuorie house which he built, and all the cities that he built, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
22.40: So Ahab slept with his fathers, and Ahaziah his sonne reigned in his stead.
22.41: And Jehoshaphat the sonne of Asa began to reign upon Judah in the fourth yeere of Ahab King of Israel.
22.42: Jehoshaphat was five and thirty yere old, when he began to reign, and reigned five and twentie yeere in Jerusalem. And his mothers name was Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.
22.43: And he walked in all the wayes of Asa his father, and declined not therefrom, but did that which was right in the eyes of the Lord. Nevertheless the hie places were not taken away: for the people offred still and burnt incense in the hie places.
22.44: And Jehoshaphat made peace with the King of Israel.
22.45: Concerning the rest of the actes of Jehoshaphat, and his worthy deedes that he did, and his battels which he fought, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
22.46: And the Sodomites, which remayned in the dayes of his father Asa, he put clean out of the land.
22.47: There was then no King in Edom: the deputie was King.
22.48: Jehoshaphat made shippes of Tharshish to sayle to Ophir for gold, but they went not, for the shippes were broken at Ezion Gaber.
22.49: Then sayde Ahaziah the sonne of Ahab unto Jehoshaphat, Let my servants goe with thy servants in the ships, But Jehoshaphat would not.
22.50: And Jehoshaphat did sleep with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the citie of David his father, and Jehoram his sonne reigned in his stead.
22.51: Ahaziah the sonne of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria, the seventeenth yeere of Jehoshaphat King of Judah, and reigned two yeeres over Israel.
22.52: But he did evil in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the way of his father, and in the way of his mother, and in the way of Jeroboam the sonne of Nebat, which made Israel to sinne.
22.53: For he served Baal and worshipped him, and provoked the Lord God of Israel unto wrath, according unto all that his father had done.
